lines.text: Hello again, %PCName. I trust I find you well. Is there anything else you'd like to ask about?

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: I am an Imperial citizen, and I believe slavery should be outlawed, as it is elsewhere in Tamriel. Many of Tamriel's people once practiced slavery, but have now rejected it as cruel and immoral. I hope that in my lifetime, slavery might be outlawed in Morrowind, but the Armistice confirmed slavery as lawful, and the Great Houses strongly resist any diminishment of the rights guaranteed by that ancient agreement between the Empire and the Dunmer.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: I am Huleeya, Assassin Service and Thrall of the Morag Tong.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: I am Huleeya. Assassin Service.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: I am in the service of the Morag Tong, a modest Thrall in rank, and by vocation and training an agent and executioner. In my private life, I am a student of history. There is little else to tell.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: I am only a low-ranking member. But pauper and commoner do not suffer from war here as they do in the West, thanks to the honored traditions of House War and the Morag Tong. I am an Argonian, yet they treat me with respect. If you are curious, find a copy of 'The Black Glove.' But please... do not mistake us for the Dark Brotherhood! The Dark Brotherhood is a perversion of ancient Dunmer traditions. They have sold their honor for profit, and are no more than a league of murderers-for-hire.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: I gave you a summary for Caius. Feel free to read it, of course.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: I welcome you as the friend of my friend, %PCName. But I wish to go to my friend's bookstore, and these troublesome fools are in my way. I have tried to persuade them, but they hate my race, and I fear there will be violence. Perhaps if you speak with them... but be careful... and be ready.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: I'm sorry, but I cannot speak with you. I am preoccupied with my own affairs.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: I'm sorry. I don't know why you'd tell me this. In the old country, they set great store by dreams and omens. But I am an educated creature. Dreams mean nothing. They are just... fancies. Imagination.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: In modern times Morrowind is ruled by five Great Houses: House Hlaalu, House Redoran, House Telvanni, House Indoril, and House Dres. Great Houses culture is partly defined by its roots in ancient Dunmer tribal clans, and partly by later Imperial  influences from other Western cultures. The Great Houses culture is only one of the native Dunmer cultures of Morrowind. The other native culture, the Ashlander culture, is a nomadic barbarian culture largely untouched by Imperial influences.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: In the First Era, the nomadic Ashlanders and the settled Dunmer clans were much alike, but after the First Council and the formation of the Great Houses, Ashlanders have been steadily forced into the poorest and most hostile lands. Now the nomadic tribes look to the prophesied return of Nerevar for a restoration of their ancient rights and religious traditions.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: In the past, some have claimed to be the reincarnated Nerevar. The most recent is known as Peakstar, a figure of legend among the Wastes tribes for the last 30 years. The Temple says these false Incarnates disprove the prophecies, since the false Incarnates fail and come to nothing, but the mystical Nerevarine cult glorifies rather than shrinks from contradictions, citing the appearance of 'failed Incarnates' as certain proof of Nerevar's coming rebirth.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: It saddens and angers me. I am sorry for their deaths, and for your trouble. But I hate the custom of despising another on account of his race, and I cannot forgive the narrowness of mind and poverty of spirit that assures them of their right to abuse and attack me for spite, or on a whim.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: I've never heard of such a thing. House Dagoth was the Sixth House, but in the War of the First Council, they betrayed the other Great Houses, and were destroyed for their treason. But I've never heard of anyone worshipping them. Dagoth Ur, the ancient head of House Dagoth, is the Devil of the Tribunal faith, but I've never heard of anyone worshipping him, either.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: I've told you what I know about the Nerevarine cult. I hope Caius finds it helpful. Is there anything else you'd like to ask about?

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: Jobasha is a friend of mine, a Khajiit. He owns Jobasha's Rare Books, which has a wide selection of rare and obscure books. He has very passionate moral and political views, which he shares freely. As a result, he and his bookshop arouse strong feelings in some quarters.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: Jobasha's Rare Books is a bookshop with a wide selection of rare and obscure books. My friend, Jobasha, a Khajiit, is the owner.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: Jobasha's Rare Books is a bookshop with a wide selection of rare and obscure books. My friend, Jobasha, a Khajiit, is the owner. The shop is here in Vivec's Foreign Quarter, in the Lower Waistworks, on the same level as the Black Shalk Cornerclub, but down at the end of the west corridor.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: Like Lord Nerevar, you have won the Battle of Red Mountain. And you bear Nerevar's great Ring, One-Clan-Under-Moon-and-Star. Will you make good Lord Nerevar's promises to the Ashlander tribes? We live in interesting times, %PCName.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: My friend, Jobasha the Khajiit, has a bookstore, Jobasha's Rare Books. He has a remarkable selection of books -- the best on Vvardenfell, I'm sure -- and he is well-educated and well-spoken, knowledgeable in local affairs.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: My friend, Jobasha the Khajiit, has a bookstore, Jobasha's Rare Books. If you will agree to travel together with me there, I will answer your questions. But before we go, I beg you to try to persuade these troublesome fools to leave us alone. Otherwise, I fear they will attack us the moment we go to leave.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: Now that Dagoth Ur is gone, there must be an end to his dark dream sendings.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: Perhaps some day, yes. For example, I would greatly wish to see the Ashlands and their peoples with my own eyes. But at present, my duties to the Morag Tong do not permit me to travel.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: Perhaps, but I do not believe you are ready.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: Thank you, %PCName. I will follow you to Jobasha's Rare Books, and we will speak further there.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: Thank you, %PCName. I will follow you to Jobasha's Rare Books, and we will speak further there.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: The Ashlanders hate the House Dunmer, who have become soft, and who have abandoned traditional ancestor worship for the gods of the Tribunal. And the Ashlanders hate outlanders, who invaded and stole their land, and forced them to live as a subject people. A reborn Nerevar who could drive out the outlander invaders, destroy the false worship of the Tribunal, and restore the pure traditional life and faith of the nomads would be a very popular hero to the Ashlanders.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: The Morag Tong executes writs and performs special duties as the ruling houses direct. Guild members never harm or steal from anyone - except the target of a legal Writ of execution. Never betray our secrets or our identities. If you break any of these rules, you must immediately speak with a Master to regain your good standing or you may be targeted for execution.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: The Morag Tong works within the system - not beyond it. We are not above the law. If you have unresolved legal issues, you should seek an officer and turn yourself in. Ultimately, the penalties will be less severe. The Morag Tong cannot afford anything but the most honorable of reputations.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: The Morag Tong works within the system - not beyond it. We are not above the law. If you have unresolved legal issues, you should seek an officer and turn yourself in. Ultimately, the penalties will be less severe. Your Writs will absolve you of any wrongdoing if you present them to the authorities.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: The sight of a free Argonian offends these racist thugs. It would tarnish my Morag Tong honor to slay them, and I don't want to trouble my friend Saralis Golmis by fighting in his club. But I must go to my friend's bookstore, where we can talk in peace. If you have a way with words, perhaps you can talk to them. Or if you have a way with money, they might be bought. Otherwise, I fear there must be bloodshed.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: The Temple treats the Nerevarine prophecies as heresy, and the Temple imprisons and executes heretics, unless prevented by Imperial law. But, since the Nerevarine cult is hostile to the Empire, the Empire does not interfere when Temple persecutes the cult. Ashlanders hate the Temple, and particularly the Ordinators, for their ruthless treatment of Nerevarine cultists.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: Their hatred saddens and angers me. I hate the custom of despising another on account of his race, and I cannot forgive the narrowness of mind and poverty of spirit that assures them of their right to abuse and attack me for spite, or on a whim.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: To understand the Nerevarine cult, you must understand the history of the Ashlanders. Nerevar means something very different to the Ashlanders from what he means to Dunmer of the Great Houses. You should also know about the persecution of the Nerevarine, and the legacy of the False Incarnate, for the Nerevarine cult is at the heart of the ancient conflict between the nomadic Ashlanders and the settled Great House Dunmer. Here is a summary for Caius, but ask your questions, and I'll answer in detail.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: Traitors to the Morag Tong must die.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: Very well, then. I will wait here for now.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: We are counted among the First Peoples. Our homeland is Argonia, or Black Marsh, in Imperial speech. I am a poor example. My parents were bound in slavery, and I have lived in Morrowind all my life. Like other Argonians who have accepted Imperial ways, I am much like any other Imperial citizen. But to be honest, we have always been a private, even secretive people, and I am not comfortable speaking in this manner. You might do better to look in books, if you are curious.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: Welcome to Vivec, %PCName. I'm Huleeya. Are you looking for services in the sacred city? Maybe I can help.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: When the Ashlanders joined Nerevar in the Battle of Red Mountain, he swore on his great Ring, One-Clan-Under-Moon-and-Star, to honor the ways of the Spirits and rights of the Land. But after the victory, Ashlanders say the power-hungry Tribunal slew Nerevar in secret. Then, setting themselves up as gods, the Tribunal and the Great Houses forgot Nerevar's promises to the Tribes. Ashlanders say Nerevar will come again with his ring, cast down the false gods, and make good his promises to the Tribes.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: Will you travel together with me to Jobasha's Rare Books? We leave the door to the Foreign Quarter Waistworks, turn right, west, continue down the hall and across the atrium on the same level, then follow the opposite corridor west on the other side of the atrium all the way to Jobasha's door. I must warn you: unless these troublesome fools are persuaded to behave like civilized beings, there may be fighting and killing if we try to travel together.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: Will you travel together with me to Jobasha's Rare Books? We leave the door to the Foreign Quarter Waistworks, turn right, west, continue down the hall and across the atrium on the same level, then follow the opposite corridor west on the other side of the atrium all the way to Jobasha's door.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: Yes, thank you very much. We should be free from distraction here. Now, I said I'd tell you about the Nerevarine cult so you can report back to Caius. And I don't know of any Sixth House cult, but I can tell you what I do know.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: Yes, you may be worthy. Your first test is to find Grandmaster Eno Hlaalu. By tradition he lives in the secret tunnels under the Arena here in Vivec. Only the Grandmaster can allow foreigners like us to join.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: Yes. I am sorry for all the trouble. If you don't mind, I'd like to go to my friend's bookstore. There I can answer all your questions.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: Yes. I simply wish to go to my friend's bookstore, but these troublesome fools are trying to threaten me. They hate my race, and I think they are spoiling for a fight. Perhaps you can speak with them, and persuade them to leave us alone. I warn you... say the wrong thing, and they may attack us both.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: Yes. We travel together to Jobasha's Rare Books. When we arrive at my friend's bookstore, I will answer your questions there.

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: You have destroyed the Devil Dagoth Ur, and ended the Blight in Morrowind. Now, I wonder, will you fulfill the other ancient prophecies of the Nerevarine? Will you drive the foreigners from the land, and restore the ancient lands and rights of the Ashlander peoples?

lines.speaker: huleeya
lines.text: You may call me Huleeya. What I do is my own affair.

lines.speaker: huzei
lines.text: I am Huzei. Slave.

lines.speaker: huzei
lines.text: You do not know? Huzei was sure... But you should be a member. If Huzei asks, 'Have you seen the Twin Lamps?' You say, 'They light the way to freedom.'

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: Are you going to bring here here? She would be safe.

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: Are you going to bring here here? She would be safe.

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: Does the Imperial cult intend to insult us thus by using such an unworthy mouthpiece to solicit alms? Leave us. Immediately.

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: Good day, Citizen %PCName. I'm Im-Kilaya. This is Ebonheart, named for Castle Ebonheart and the Duke of Ebonheart, Duke Vedam Dren, by the grace of our Emperor, the Emperor's representative here in Vvardenfell District. Can I help you ?

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: Grace of the Nine, Citizen %PCName. I'm Im-Kilaya. Welcome to Ebonheart, capital of Vvardenfell District. Are you looking for someone in particular?

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: Greeting, Citizen %PCName. I'm Im-Kilaya. Can I help you? This your first visit to Ebonheart? Is there some specific place you seek?

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: If you will check your records, citizen, you will see that the province of Argonia has already given alms for the poor.

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: It is good that you brought her here. We have heard tales of drugs being smuggled inside these poor people. There seems to be no low the smugglers and slavers won't stoop to for profit. We will give her the help she needs. Thank you, and please take this in return. Perhaps it will help you in funding other missions of goodwill. Take care.

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: Reeh-Jah? He sounds like one of our people, but I do not know him myself.

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: She is in good hands now. Thank you, %PCName.

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: Thank you for bringing this to our attention. Surely someone has exceeded his authority, and jeopardized our Mission by disregarding the unjust laws of this land. I trust you will not mention this to others, since you are admittedly eager to maintain our good will.

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: Thank you for bringing this to our attention. Surely someone has exceeded his authority, and jeopardized our Mission by disregarding the unjust laws of this land. I trust you will not mention this to others, since you are admittedly eager to maintain our good will.

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: The Imperial cult has our respect. But we are disappointed that the Imperial cult does not speak out against the inhumane practices of slavery in Morrowind. We take this disappointment into consideration when determining the generosity of our support. I'm afraid we have no donation to offer at this time.

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: The Imperial cult has our respect. We are disappointed that the Imperial cult does not speak out against the inhumane practices of slavery in Morrowind. But perhaps you are right. It is by demonstrating our superior commitment to civilization and humanity that we best disprove the Dunmer's barbaric insistence that we are no more than animals. Please accept this donation to the Imperial cult on behalf of the province of Argonia, with our thanks.

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: The Imperial cult has our respect. We are disappointed that the Imperial cult does not speak out against the inhumane practices of slavery in Morrowind. But we agree with you, that this is not sufficient reason to cause the needy to suffer for want of our province's generosity. Therefore, we ask you to accept this donation as alms for the poor on behalf of the province of Argonia.

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: We heard of the death of this poor slave. At least he did not die in captivity.

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: We heard the slave had been killed. This is a very sad thing.

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: We will get him back to his people. Soon, by the Root, he will be back among his people, with the sweet smell of the Hist making fire in his veins.

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: Welcome, Citizen %PCName. I'm Im-Kilaya, and this is Ebonheart. If you're new here, you'll be wanting to ask about our many services for travelers. And I imagine you wouldn't mind a little advice?

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: We've heard you returned that poor man to his captors. Do you know what happened to him after you brought him in? No? They had him flogged until the skin was flayed from his back. No, he's not dead. That would be too easy, you see, and he wouldn't bring a profit. They healed him, so they could flog him again. That's how the slavers serve notice to their slaves that escape is not an option. I hope you feel pride in your work. Get out of here, %PCRace. Get out while you can.

lines.speaker: Im_Kilaya
lines.text: You have done a good thing here, %PCName. You have helped one of our people with no promise of reward, and at great peril to yourself. I see good things for you if you continue on this path. The lamps burn brightly for you, I can see that. Take this as a show of our gratitude.

lines.speaker: inee
lines.text: And good day to you, %PCName. I'm Inee. I assume you're new to Sadrith Mora, since we've never spoken before. I know most everyone in town. Can I help you find someone in particular?

lines.speaker: inee
lines.text: I am Inee. Slave.

lines.speaker: inee
lines.text: Yes. I'm Inee. Go ahead. I'm sure you have questions.

lines.speaker: inee
lines.text: You do not know? Inee was sure... But you should be a member. If Inee asks, 'Have you seen the Twin Lamps?' You say, 'They light the way to freedom.'

lines.speaker: itan
lines.text: Greetings, Citizen. I'm Itan. This town is Balmora, Council Seat of House Hlaalu. We're loyal citizens of the Empire, and proud of it. Well, most of us, anyway. So, are you looking for someone in particular? Are you looking for services? Is there some specific place you'd like to visit? Would you like me to tell you about my trade?

lines.speaker: itan
lines.text: Greetings, Citizen. I'm Itan. This town is Balmora, Council Seat of House Hlaalu. We're loyal citizens of the Empire, and proud of it. Well, most of us, anyway. So, are you looking for someone in particular? Are you looking for services? Is there some specific place you'd like to visit? Would you like me to tell you about my trade?

lines.speaker: itan
lines.text: Greetings, Citizen. I'm Itan. Welcome to Balmora. We're a House Hlaalu town, and loyal citizens of the Empire. What can I do for you?

lines.speaker: itan
lines.text: Hello, %PCName. I'm Itan, and this is Balmora. I don't believe we've met. Is there something I can do for you?

lines.speaker: itan
lines.text: Hello, friend. I'm Itan. Welcome to Balmora. If you have a question, I'll be happy to answer it. Or try, anyway. And if it's just a little advice you'd like, that's fine, too.

lines.speaker: itan
lines.text: I am Itan. Commoner.

lines.speaker: itan
lines.text: So, your name is %PCName? And you're new here in Balmora? Well, my name is Itan. And I don't mind answering questions. I have nothing else on my mind right now. And if I start to bore you about Morrowind lore, just let me know.

lines.speaker: jeelus-tei
lines.text: I am Jeelus-Tei. Slave.

lines.speaker: jeelus-tei
lines.text: I'm fine, thank you, %PCName. You can call me Jeelus-Tei. First visit to Suran? We get lots of pilgrims here, since the birthplace of Molag Bal and Fields of Kummu nearby are a popular pilgrimage sites. Is there some specific place you'd like to see?

lines.speaker: jeelus-tei
lines.text: I'm Jeelus-Tei. This is the village of Suran, gateway to Bal Ur. Are you looking for services here? Or was there something else I can do for you?

lines.speaker: jeelus-tei
lines.text: Pleased to meet you. I'm Jeelus-Tei. New here? I'm sure you have some questions for me.

lines.speaker: jeelus-tei
lines.text: Welcome to Suran, gem of the Ascadian Isles. I'm Jeelus-Tei. What brings you to our fair village? Are you looking for someone in particular?

lines.speaker: jeelus-tei
lines.text: You do not know? Jeelus-Tei was sure... But you should be a member. If Jeelus-Tei asks, 'Have you seen the Twin Lamps?' You say, 'They light the way to freedom.'

lines.speaker: jeer-maht
lines.text: I am Jeer-Maht. Slave.

lines.speaker: jeer-maht
lines.text: You do not know? Jeer-Maht was sure... But you should be a member. If Jeer-Maht asks, 'Have you seen the Twin Lamps?' You say, 'They light the way to freedom.'

lines.speaker: j'ram-dar
lines.text: I am J'Ram-Dar. Slave.

lines.speaker: j'ram-dar
lines.text: You do not know? J'Ram-Dar was sure... But you should be a member. If J'Ram-Dar asks, 'Have you seen the Twin Lamps?' You say, 'They light the way to freedom.'

lines.speaker: junal_lei
lines.text: I am Junal-Lei. Acrobat.

lines.speaker: keerasa_tan
lines.text: I am Keerasa-Tan. Slave.

lines.speaker: keerasa_tan
lines.text: You do not know? Keerasa-Tan was sure... But you should be a member. If Keerasa-Tan asks, 'Have you seen the Twin Lamps?' You say, 'They light the way to freedom.'

lines.speaker: lord cluttermonkey
lines.text: I am Lord Cluttermonkey. Farmer.

lines.speaker: meer
lines.text: I am Meer. Slave.

lines.speaker: meer
lines.text: You do not know? Meer was sure... But you should be a member. If Meer asks, 'Have you seen the Twin Lamps?' You say, 'They light the way to freedom.'

lines.speaker: miun_gei
lines.text: Almsivi, %PCName. I'm Miun-Gei. Don't worry. Vivec can be confusing for us, and we live here. Is there some specific place you want? Or someone in particular you're trying to find?

lines.speaker: miun_gei
lines.text: Did you not see him as you entered? It is that Marcel Maurard. Outside my shop he stands all day, selling ridiculous wares. Get rid of him I would like to, but the law says he is within his rights. Perhaps you might find a way?

lines.speaker: miun_gei
lines.text: He won't be a problem any longer.

lines.speaker: miun_gei
lines.text: I don't know anything. I swear.

lines.speaker: miun_gei
lines.text: Look, I only had one contact in the Brotherhood, a Khajiit named Tsrazami. But she's dead, and I'm not a member myself.

lines.speaker: miun_gei
lines.text: No? Perhaps you have not the skill. I understand. Maybe he will die a horrible death and all will be made right. It is possible, you know.

lines.speaker: miun_gei
lines.text: Oh, how I detest that ridiculous man.

lines.speaker: miun_gei
lines.text: Welcome to Vivec, %PCName. I'm Miun-Gei. Are you looking for services in the sacred city? Maybe I can help.

lines.speaker: miun_gei
lines.text: Welcome, %PCRace. It is good to see a customer in the store. That annoying fool outside chases them away.

lines.speaker: miun_gei
lines.text: You don't act like a guard, so I'll tell you. My contact in the Brotherhood is Tsrazami, a Khajiit. She's in the Plaza here in the Foreign Quarter. Tell her I sent you.

lines.speaker: miun_gei
lines.text: You killed him? Well, I suppose that's one way of taking of that problem. But now I'll have the guards around here asking questions, harassing my customers. I don't need that at all. I appreciate you getting rid of him, but there had to be another way. Anyway, take this. And you didn't get it from me.

lines.speaker: miun_gei
lines.text: You think you can? I would like that. Make him go away, an I will have rewards for you!

lines.speaker: miun_gei
lines.text: You want to hire the Dark Brotherhood? How do I know I can trust you?

lines.speaker: miun_gei
lines.text: You've done it! I admire your persuasiveness, friend. Thank you for your help. Allow me to give you this as a token of my appreciation.

lines.speaker: morning_clouds
lines.text: I am Morning-Star-Steals-Away-Clouds. Slave.

lines.speaker: morning_clouds
lines.text: To the north and west I have heard, but it is just stories that are told.

lines.speaker: morning_clouds
lines.text: You do not know? Morning-Star-Steals-Away-Clouds was sure... But you should be a member. If Morning-Star-Steals-Away-Clouds asks, 'Have you seen the Twin Lamps?' You say, 'They light the way to freedom.'

lines.speaker: mush_mere
lines.text: I am Mush-Mere. Pauper.

lines.speaker: mush_mere
lines.text: I'm Mush-Mere. And this is Gnaar Mok. And you're... %PCName? Fine. That's all taken care of. Now. Why don't you tell me what you want?

lines.speaker: mush_mere
lines.text: I'm Mush-Mere. Never seen you here before. First time in Gnaar Mok, then. Let me give you a little advice. We aren't used to visitors here, and we don't like what we aren't used to. So don't be surprised if people don't like answering a lot of questions. But you seem an okay sort. So if you are looking for someone in particular, or looking for services, or looking for a specific place, go ahead and ask.

lines.speaker: Neetinei
lines.text: I am Neetinei. Slave.

lines.speaker: Neetinei
lines.text: You do not know? Neetinei was sure... But you should be a member. If Neetinei asks, 'Have you seen the Twin Lamps?' You say, 'They light the way to freedom.'

lines.speaker: Nelix Fly-Breath
lines.text: I am Nelix Fly-Breath. Smuggler.

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: Hello again. Is this about my trade. Or are you here for a little advice? Or Morrowind lore? Or the latest rumors?

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: Welcome. Nine-Toes is my name, Hunter is my trade. I'd be happy to share a little advice or Morrowind lore with a fellow Blade. Or maybe you'd like to catch up on the latest rumors?

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: Greetings, Citizen. I'm Nine-Toes. This town is Balmora, Council Seat of House Hlaalu. We're loyal citizens of the Empire, and proud of it. Well, most of us, anyway. So, are you looking for someone in particular? Are you looking for services? Is there some specific place you'd like to visit? Would you like me to tell you about my trade?

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: Greetings, Citizen. I'm Nine-Toes. This town is Balmora, Council Seat of House Hlaalu. We're loyal citizens of the Empire, and proud of it. Well, most of us, anyway. So, are you looking for someone in particular? Are you looking for services? Is there some specific place you'd like to visit? Would you like me to tell you about my trade?

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: Greetings, Citizen. I'm Nine-Toes. Welcome to Balmora. We're a House Hlaalu town, and loyal citizens of the Empire. What can I do for you?

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: Hello, %PCName. I'm Nine-Toes, and this is Balmora. I don't believe we've met. Is there something I can do for you?

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: Hello, friend. I'm Nine-Toes. Welcome to Balmora. If you have a question, I'll be happy to answer it. Or try, anyway. And if it's just a little advice you'd like, that's fine, too.

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: I am Nine-Toes, Hunter and Journeyman of the Blades.

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: I am Nine-Toes. Hunter.

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: I have heard the rumors, but I am not a murderer. I believe someone is spreading these rumors because I am a foreigner and an Argonian.

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: I heard you found the real murderer. I am grateful to you, soft-skin.

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: I heard you found the real murderer. It is good to trust each other among these slavers, %PCName.

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: I'm a Blade, too, and I report to Caius, like you. You're welcome to use my bed to rest, but leave my other stuff alone, please.

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: I'm trying to update our maps of the Bitter Coast. There are no goods maps of this area. Period. Islands, mountains, swamps, lakes, rivers. It's impossible. I'm getting to know the swamps and waterways here, maybe as well as the natives. But I can't blend with the natives, and I'm useless in the West Gash or the Ashlands. And I don't see why the maps are so important. Smuggling, maybe. But I'm wondering if they're thinking about landing and moving the Legions through here. In case of trouble.

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: See? Now you know I am innocent.

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: So, your name is %PCName? And you're new here in Balmora? Well, my name is Nine-Toes. And I don't mind answering questions. I have nothing else on my mind right now. And if I start to bore you about Morrowind lore, just let me know.

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: The basics we can teach you, won't cost much. Advanced training, though... that's expensive. If you're already skilled, you're much harder to teach. Maybe I can help you out. Here's a little moon sugar, on the house. You do know that trade in moon sugar and skooma is against the law, and most alchemists and apothecaries won't buy it. But Khajiit generally will. Try Ajira at the Balmora Mages Guild, or Ra'Virr, the trader in Balmora. Sell the sugar, and start saving for training.

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: Yes, I am Nine-Toes.

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: Yes, I offer training, but only to Blades.

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: Yes, we heard Caius had been recalled. He said we'd still be forwarding our reports to him. I think he thought what you're doing is important -- whatever it is -- he didn't tell us -- and we weren't supposed to bother you.

lines.speaker: nine_toes
lines.text: You must have been misinformed. I don't offer services to the public.

lines.speaker: Okan_Shei
lines.text: Good day, Citizen %PCName. I'm Okan-Shei. This is Ebonheart, named for Castle Ebonheart and the Duke of Ebonheart, Duke Vedam Dren, by the grace of our Emperor, the Emperor's representative here in Vvardenfell District. Can I help you ?

lines.speaker: Okan_Shei
lines.text: Grace of the Nine, Citizen %PCName. I'm Okan-Shei. Welcome to Ebonheart, capital of Vvardenfell District. Are you looking for someone in particular?

lines.speaker: Okan_Shei
lines.text: Greeting, Citizen %PCName. I'm Okan-Shei. Can I help you? This your first visit to Ebonheart? Is there some specific place you seek?

lines.speaker: Okan_Shei
lines.text: He doesn't work here anymore, and I don't think the Company wants us to discuss him with outsiders.

lines.speaker: Okan_Shei
lines.text: I am Okan-Shei. Savant.

lines.speaker: Okan_Shei
lines.text: Welcome, Citizen %PCName. I'm Okan-Shei, and this is Ebonheart. If you're new here, you'll be wanting to ask about our many services for travelers. And I imagine you wouldn't mind a little advice?

lines.speaker: Okan_Shei
lines.text: You know, I think he had a Telvanni girlfriend. He kept her a secret. I don't know why. But I saw them together once in the Foreign Quarter at Vivec. She was quite attractive.

lines.speaker: Okaw
lines.text: I am Okaw. Slave.

lines.speaker: Okaw
lines.text: You do not know? Okaw was sure... But you should be a member. If Okaw asks, 'Have you seen the Twin Lamps?' You say, 'They light the way to freedom.'

lines.text: I am Oleen-Gei. Slave.

lines.speaker: oleen-gei
lines.text: You do not know? Oleen-Gei was sure... But you should be a member. If Oleen-Gei asks, 'Have you seen the Twin Lamps?' You say, 'They light the way to freedom.'

lines.speaker: olink-nur
lines.text: You do not know? Olink-Nur was sure... But you should be a member. If Olink-Nur asks, 'Have you seen the Twin Lamps?' You say, 'They light the way to freedom.'

lines.text: Do you want training, %PCName?
