You should know the Empire's attitudes about killing. According to Imperial law and custom, killing is justifiable in war, self-defense, defense of property, affairs of honor, and sanctioned affairs of state. Other killings are murder, and punishable by death or imprisonment. Outlaws have no rights, and may be killed without scandal or sanction. Guards may use deadly force in the line of duty.
You should speak with one of the Masters of the Morag Tong. They may allow you to clear your name.
You should speak with one of the Stewards: Sugar-Lips Habasi, Aengoth the Jeweler, Big Helende, or Gentleman Jim Stacey.
You should speak with the monk An-Deesei at the Argonian Mission. If the monk's life interests you, that is.
You still here? What do you want now? Are you looking for a specific place here in Seyda Neen?
You still in Molag Mar? What do you want from me?
You think so, do you? Perhaps you want to prove it?
You think you're being clever, %PCName. But I know what you're up to.
You turned in one of our best spies, Elmussa Damori. I'm not giving you anything unless you order me, and you don't outrank me.
You want something I suppose? Here in Suran?
You want something, stranger? Are you lost? This is the village of Suran.
You want to hire a wizard as a guard? Talk to Arielle Phiencel.
You want to see Orvas Dren? He's in his villa, on the east side of the plantation.
You want to speak with me about advancement? Am I ready for the next rank, Arch-Mage?
You want to talk? Fine. What shall we talk about? My trade? I can talk about that. When you've heard enough, let me know.
You will get slaughtered if you start acting like a warrior. Always sneak up to your target and take advantage of your stealth. Even a dagger is effective if used in the right way at the right time.
You will have to get rid of that Moon Sugar if you want any services from me. I don't want any trouble.
You will have to get rid of that Moon Sugar if you want any services from me. I don't want any trouble.
You won't believe what old Avus said yesterday. 'I could live in a nutshell and be consumed with infinite space were it not that I have bad dreams.' What the hell is he talking about?
You won't make many friends with an attitude like yours.
You won't win any popularity contests here, outlander. What's your problem, anyway?
You would lose.

You'd think she'd be more discreet, seeing as how the Duke's her father. But Ilmene Dren is a strong-willed young woman, and she hates slavery with a passion. Her family's wealth and influence means nothing to her. She's proud of living in a St. Delyn slum. And she doesn't mind being seen with known abolitionists like that bookseller, Jobasha.
You'd want Vala. She's around here somewhere. She accepts all the book donations.
You'll be sorry you said that, %PCRace.
You'll find her shack on the west side of town.
You'll find his shop in the Plaza of the Foreign Quarter.
You'll find it Under-Skar. That's the giant shell on the north side of town, outlander.
You'll find it Under-Skar. That's the giant shell on the north side of town, outlander.
You'll find it Under-Skar. That's the giant shell on the north side of town, outlander.
You'll find Mages Guild halls in Balmora, Ald'ruhn, Caldera, Wolverine Hall in Sadrith Mora, and the Foreign Quarter in Vivec.
You'll find the glacier in the northwest part of Solstheim. Very little lives in the area, and it is said that the glacier itself is haunted by evil spirits.

You'll find the smith Bols Indalen at Craftmen's Hall in Godsreach, along with several other fine craftsmen. There's a healer and an Imperial altar in the Royal Palace. Go to the Temple for Temple services. Otherwise, most trainers, crafters, and merchants are in the Great Bazaar.
You'll find them all over this island. Be careful, though. Some of them carry diseases!

You'll find Zeno Faustus in the Armory. He'll repair your weapons or sell you a new one. If you're sick, try the Imperial Cult Shrine. For a small donation, you can usually get a cure for what ails you.
You'll need the key to free me of my bonds.
You'll regret trying to bribe me.

Your first visit to Morrowind, outlander? Then learn the law and local customs. Get a copy of Law and Custom in Morrowind. Slavery is legal here. Foul murder is illegal, but if he strikes the first blow, you're in the clear. A verbal attack is illegal, just like an unprovoked physical attack. Folks are touchy about personal honor. Watch your tongue, or you'll get called out to a duel.
Your kind is not welcome here, vampire. Ask me what you will, and be on your way.
Your manner is offensive, %PCRace. I must object.
Your outfit is quite impressive, %PCName. Can I help you?
Your reputation precedes you, %PCName. And it won't win you any friends here in Ebonheart.
Your threat comes from a weak, limp bag.
Your tone lacks sincerity.
Your troubles with the law are none of my business, but don't try anything with me.
Your troubles with the law are none of my business, but don't try anything with me.
Your troubles with the law are none of my business, but don't try anything with me.
Your words are hollow. Stop this.
Your words, they make me feel, well, special.

You're a freelance adventurer, yes? If you're looking for challenge, try Esutanamus, a Daedric shrine on an offshore island to the southeast, or Nchuleft, a Dwemer ruin to the southeast where the plains and the slopes of Red Mountain meet. They're large ruins -- easy to find.

You're a freelance adventurer, yes? There're many tombs, ruins, and lairs in the Grazelands to the south and west. Just keep your eyes open. They're often marked by a clump of rocks or trees at the entrance.
You're a known criminal, %PCName. I will have nothing to do with you until you have cleared your name.
You're a long way from home, stranger. If you're looking for some specific place in Molag Mar, I might be able to help you.

You're a new face. So what can I tell you about Balmora? I like to swap the latest rumors, when there's something juicy enough to gossip about. Or, maybe, if you have a little secret, maybe I have one to trade.
You're about as popular as a bowl of tar. And whose fault is that? It's your fault, outlander.

You're an adventurer, right? Then watch out if you go down in the sewers. That's the way to the ruins of Old Mournhold, yes, and that's where an adventurer can make his fortune. But... the Black Dart Gang preys on adventurers down below. They look harmless -- like outcasts or beggars. You may think you're tough... you can handle anything. But not the Black Dart Gang.
You're an adventurer? Then you carry cure poison, dispel, and restore fatigue potions, as well as levitate and restore health potions. Right?
You're back. You forget something?
You're in Ald'ruhn, stranger. Are you looking for someone in particular?
You're in Balmora. Go ahead and ask your question.
You're in Fort Frostmoth, jewel of the Empire. Get out while you can.
You're in Gnaar Mok. Go ahead. You ask the questions, and I'll do the answering.

You're in the Royal Palace now. South is Plaza Brindisi Dorom. North is the Temple Courtyard and Almalexia's Temple. To the west is Godsreach, to the east is the Great Bazaar -- but you can't get there from here -- go through the Temple or Plaza first.
You're looking for muck? Ask Anis Seloth here in town. Her shop is on the north side of town, next to Fara's Hole in the Wall.
You're looking well. Is there something you need?
You're new here, outlander. If you want someone in particular, ask.
You're new here, right? Are you looking for services? Or what?
You're new to Ald'ruhn, right? Are you looking for services in town?
You're new to Molag Mar, right? What do you want here? You looking for someone in particular?
You're new to Suran, right? Are you looking for services here?
You're not from around here. Something you want to ask me about Balmora?
You're not looking so good. Sick, I mean. You probably want to go to the Imperial Shrine and get that taken care of.
You're not so bad yourself.
You're not supposed to be here, Hlaalu
You're not supposed to be here, Redoran.
You're not supposed to be here, Telvanni
You're not the type I like to deal with.
You're not well. You should get yourself cured.
You're not worth killing.
You're so nice. You must want something.
You're spoiling my day. Leave me alone.
You're still in Sadrith Mora, eh? What do you want now?

You're still poking around in Seyda Neen? What do you want now?
You're the new Archmage, %PCName. Try and forget about Trebonius.
You're the one who killed them? Netch are valuable, but they're too dangerous to let them roam free. Thank you.
You're there. What do you want?
You're too kind.
You're too kind. I can't refuse such a friendly gesture.
You're upsetting me. Can't we resolve this in a civil manner?
You're wasting your breath.
You're wasting your time. I won't be bullied.
You're welcome.
Yours is not a familiar face, stranger. You come to Gnisis for something in particular?
You've been expelled from the guild. Take care of that, and maybe we can talk.
You've chosen your own death.
You've come to the right person. At least, I hope I can answer your questions.
You've got a disease that I've not seen before. It must have been brought here by you or one of the Imperials. Get it cured. Now. We don't want your diseases in this place.
You've got some sort of disease. Something's just not right with you. And that's not a good sign around here.
You've got the blight disease. Must have picked it up on Vvardenfell. You'll want to get that taken care of quickly.
You've got the blight disease. You must have come over here recently from the big island. Get that taken care of. We don't need it around here.
You've got the corprus! Stay away from me. I've heard there's no cure for that. You should head back to Vvardenfell. We don't need that at the fort.

You've heard about it? I saw it myself. Open the South Turret bed chamber door and there it is. Another fellow went in an attacked it. He wasn't badly hurt, and it wasn't hard to drive it away. But a couple hours later, someone else went up there and it was back. And it KEEPS coming back, no matter what you do. Neloth's Mouth, Arara Uvulas the mage, looked at it, but he doesn't know what's happening. The Gateway can't rent the room, and Angaredhel is very upset.
